invented: Claims that 31G in tmp proves cleanup is broken or missing.
errors: Git retention is oversimplified: unreachable reflog entries normally expire after 30 days, and refs other than branches also retain objects.
Immediate pruning on a live repository can race concurrent Git operations; the plan does not address this.
Claims deleted branches cannot be recovered after expiry and GC, although their commits may remain reachable through other refs.
A.note: The staged approval process is clear, but the proposed Git cleanup is unnecessarily aggressive and its recovery claims are inaccurate.

invented: Says the user did not list Docker, although the task lists /var/lib/docker.
Claims to be running on the user's WSL machine.
errors: Recent modification does not establish that a file is an active upload, and an old timestamp does not establish that deletion is safe.
Changing Docker daemon logging defaults and restarting does not apply those defaults to existing containers; affected containers need recreation.
A Docker restart is not guaranteed to cause only a momentary app interruption.
B.note: The conservative commands and per-step approval make this the strongest plan, despite invented environment details and no clear warning that tmp deletion is irreversible.

invented: Claims the current session is WSL.
errors: Reflog expiry is not always required to reclaim objects after branch deletion, and refs other than branches can retain commits.
Immediate pruning on a live repository can race concurrent Git operations; the plan does not address this.
The reflog-expiry and GC commands do not specify /srv/app or establish that it is the working directory.
C.note: It asks useful safety questions, but assumes Docker will be a large safe win and offers aggressive Git commands before establishing their need.

invented: Claims that 31G in tmp proves nothing removes old files there.
errors: Uploads in progress do not necessarily have fresh modification timestamps, so age alone cannot protect them.
No gain after deletion does not prove a process holds the files open; other causes include concurrent disk growth and snapshots.
Reflog expiry is not always a prerequisite for reclaiming objects after branch deletion.
D.note: The plan is readable and conservative about Docker, but overstates what timestamps prove and lacks an explicit irreversibility warning.
